- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for high sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — increase forecast by 1–3% for low sentiment periods.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price increases — cap forecast growth at 2–4% above prior peak unless sentiment confirms strong bullish momentum.
- Allow for mean reversion in 3–5 day windows — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is mixed or declining (0.3–0.7) — avoid overconfidence in sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment trap” overreaction.
